content: The following studies and reports provide insights into various aspects of HIV prevention, treatment, and service delivery, particularly in lowand middle-income countries: 1. Nalubamba et al. (2016) conducted a randomized evaluation in Zambia to assess the cost-effectiveness of referral and linkage models for HIV and sexual and reproductive health services. 2. Siapka et al. (2017) examined the impact of integrating sexual and reproductive health services on consultation duration times, as part of the Integra Initiative. 3. Birdthistle et al. (2014) analyzed client flow data over time in Swaziland to evaluate the integration of HIV and maternal healthcare in a high HIV-prevalence setting. 4. Obure et al. (2016) investigated whether integrating HIV and sexual and reproductive health services improves technical efficiency in Kenya and Swaziland using a two-stage semi-parametric approach. 5. Siapka et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review to explore the potential for cost savings and efficiency gains in HIV services in lowand middle-income countries. 6. Obure et al. (2016) analyzed the economies of scale and scope achieved through the integration of HIV and sexual and reproductive health services under the Integra Initiative. 7. Ayon et al. (2019) developed integrated community-based services for HIV prevention, harm reduction, and sexual and reproductive health targeting women who inject drugs. 8. Dulli et al. (2019) implemented a non-randomized trial in Kenya to address broader reproductive health needs of female sex workers through integrated family planning and HIV prevention services. 9. Milford et al. (2018) explored healthcare providers' understanding and attitudes toward implementing an integrated HIV and sexual and reproductive health service model in South Africa. 10. Narasimhan et al. (2018) emphasized the importance of investing in the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women and girls to achieve HIV and universal health coverage (UHC) goals. 11. Sarkis et al. (2015) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to determine the prevalence of hypertension in lowand middle-income countries. 12. Ameh et al. (2017) evaluated the effectiveness of an integrated approach to HIV and hypertension care in rural South Africa using a controlled interrupted time-series analysis. 13. Rawat et al. (2018) assessed the influence of integrating HIV care into primary healthcare clinics on diabetes and hypertension care in South Africa over four years. 14. Fairall et al. (2016) conducted a pragmatic cluster randomized controlled trial in South Africa to evaluate an educational outreach intervention for nurse-led management of chronic non-communicable diseases. 15. Prabhakaran et al. (2019) tested the effectiveness of an mHealth-based electronic decision support system for managing chronic conditions in primary care through the mWellcare trial. 16. Havlir et al. (2019) implemented a community health approach for HIV testing and treatment in rural Africa, demonstrating its impact on HIV care outcomes. 17. Rohwer et al. (2018) reviewed the effects of integrated care models for diabetes and hypertension in lowand middle-income countries. 18. Kemp et al. (2018) conducted a systematic review on the integration of HIV and non-communicable disease services in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on implementation science. 19. Rabkin et al. (2018) highlighted the need to strengthen the health workforce to support the integration of HIV and non-communicable disease services in sub-Saharan Africa. 20. Chang et al. (2016) evaluated the cost and efficiency of a hybrid mobile multi-disease testing approach with high HIV testing coverage in East Africa. 21. Venables et al. (2016) explored the acceptability of integrated medication adherence clubs for HIV and non-communicable disease patients in Kibera, Kenya. 22. Achmad et al. (2009) studied the integration of methadone maintenance treatment and HIV care for injecting drug users in Bandung, Indonesia. 23. Lucas et al. (2010) compared clinic-based treatment of opioid-dependent HIV-infected patients with referral to an opioid treatment program in a randomized trial. 24. Zaller et al. (2007) proposed a model of integrated primary care for HIV-positive patients with substance use and mental illness. 25. Low et al. (2016) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the impact of opioid substitution therapy on antiretroviral therapy outcomes. 26. Guise et al. (2017) synthesized client and provider experiences with integrated opioid substitution therapy and HIV care through a qualitative systematic review. 27. Ndlovu et al. (2018) conducted a feasibility study on multi-disease testing for HIV and TB using the GeneXpert platform in rural Zimbabwe. 28. Fox and Rosen (2013) systematically reviewed pediatric retention on HIV treatment in lowand middle-income countries between 2008 and 2013. 29. Mutambo and Hlongwana (2019) explored healthcare workers' perspectives on barriers to providing HIV services to children in sub-Saharan Africa. 30. Nyandiko et al. (2006) analyzed outcomes of HIV-infected orphaned and non-orphaned children on antiretroviral therapy in western Kenya. 31. Wilkinson et al. (2018) evaluated the outcomes of children receiving antiretroviral therapy in family adherence clubs in Khayelitsha, South Africa. 32. Wanga et al. (2019) assessed the acceptability of community-based mentor mothers supporting HIV-positive pregnant women on antiretroviral therapy in Kenya. 33. Vreeman et al. 34. Denison et al. (2015) explored perspectives of adolescents living with HIV and their caregivers on adherence to antiretroviral therapy and self-management. 35. Mavhu et al. (2020) evaluated the effect of a differentiated service delivery model on virological failure in adolescents with HIV in Zimbabwe. These studies collectively highlight the importance of integrated care models, community-based interventions, and tailored approaches to improve HIV prevention, treatment, and care outcomes across diverse populations and settings.
